slides.title: He's never left Pakistan. He's already living globally.
slides.brief: Stark moody cinematic close-up, shot on Sony A7 IV, 85mm f/1.4, available light. A Pakistani university student, male, 21, sitting cross-legged on grass — LUMS lawn, palm trees soft-focus in background, golden afternoon light. He's wearing a faded vintage oversized tee, wireless earbuds in. His phone screen dominates the left third of the frame — held up at a natural angle, screen fully visible and hyper-realistic: Netflix app open, playing a Korean drama, Korean subtitles visible, progress bar at 47 minutes. On the right side of his lap: an open takeout container with Korean ramen, chopsticks resting on the edge. His expression is completely absorbed — not performing for anyone, just living it. He doesn't own a passport. He's never left Pakistan. On the dark grassy ground below him, in bold white stencil type casting a faint shadow: "HE'S NEVER LEFT PAKISTAN. HE'S ALREADY LIVING GLOBALLY." Fine subtext beneath: "73% of Pakistani Gen Z consume foreign culture daily. Food is next." Cinematic color grade: warm golden-hour tones, slight teal in the shadows. Heavy film grain.

slides.title: We didn't wait for Pakistan to discover the world.
slides.brief: Hyper-dramatic cinematic photograph render, shot on Leica SL2, 35mm, available light only. Interior of a Pakistan Airlines cabin — warm overhead cabin lighting, real economy seat textures, tray tables down. Tight on a single Pakistani woman, mid-20s, dupatta loosely around her shoulders, AirPods in — she's holding a premium matte black Knorr Global Flavors noodle cup with both hands, steam rising directly into the cabin light above, her eyes closed in genuine involuntary pleasure, head tilted slightly back. The cup's Knorr red branding and "Global Flavors" text are crisp and readable. Through the oval window beside her: clouds at 35,000 feet, golden hour light bleeding in. In the seat behind her, barely in focus: another passenger mid-slurp, phone up filming themselves eating. Floating in the upper left in large white condensed stencil typography against the dark cabin ceiling: "WE DIDN'T WAIT FOR PAKISTAN TO DISCOVER THE WORLD." Fine white subtext beneath: "Phase 1: Knorr Global Flavors. Live. In-flight. First in Pakistan." Cinematic color grade: warm amber-gold on subjects, deep cool blue in the cabin shadows. Heavy film grain. Deep vignette on all four edges.

slides.title: Three pins. One campaign.
slides.brief: Stark deeply moody cinematic top-down photograph render, Leica SL2, 50mm Noctilux f/0.95, single overhead spotlight. A large weathered paper map of Karachi spread flat across a dark aged oak table — street grids, DHA, Gulshan, university locations all legible, slightly yellowed at the edges, one fold crease running diagonally. Three oversized antique brass map pins driven firmly into the map — each carrying a small rectangular white card flag on a thin wire: PIN 1 placed over a university cluster, flag reading "PLACE" in bold dark condensed type, subtext in tiny caps: "Show up where they live." PIN 2 placed over a food street zone, flag reading "PARTICIPATION", subtext: "Make the experience the content." PIN 3 placed over a dense residential area, flag reading "PROOF", subtext: "Real reactions. Real volume." A single red thread connects all three pins, pulled taut in a triangle, casting a thin shadow on the map. Around the map on the table: a Knorr Global Flavors boarding pass card — printed, premium stock, "DESTINATION: SEOUL" visible. A smartphone lying face-up, screen showing Instagram Reels recording interface — red record button active, live view showing a steaming noodle bowl. A single printed sheet — bar chart, impressions line spiking sharply upward, "5M+" annotated at the peak. One overhead industrial pendant lamp casting a perfect circle of warm amber light on the map center, everything beyond the lamp radius falling into near-total darkness. Floating in the dark upper zone of the frame in large white condensed stencil bold: "THREE PINS. ONE CAMPAIGN." Fine white subtext beneath: "Place. Participation. Proof." Cinematic color grade: warm amber on the map, cool dark shadows everywhere else. Heavy film grain. Deep vignette on all edges.
